rulers.name: Harthacnut (Cnut III)
rulers.note: Infobox: king of Denmark from 12 November 1035 to 8 June 1042 and of England 1040 to 8 June 1042.

keyframe_review.note: 215,699 km2, the same bounding box as the 1018 North Sea Empire shape (England and Denmark). Neither page opened gives an area. The shape runs 1040-1045 but the union lasted only from Harthacnut's landing at Sandwich on 17 June 1040 to his death on 8 June 1042: he 'was succeeded by Magnus in Denmark and Edward the Confessor in England'. For 1043-1045 England belongs to the Kingdom of England (Cliopatria's England row has no shape between 1018 and 1045, a Cliopatria gap) and Denmark to Magnus (see norway-denmark). The title Cliopatria gives this row, 'Danish attacks on Norman England', is the article on the raids of 1069-1085 and says nothing about 1040-1045 (H2).

correction.text: unchanged shape; the years should read 1040..1042 (17 June 1040 to 8 June 1042); England and Denmark part in 1042

region.text: Denmark, already Harthacnut's, and England, which he reached in June 1040

ledger.note: 17 June 1040: Harthacnut lands at Sandwich and rules England and Denmark together. H1: 'Harold died on 17 March 1040 and soon afterwards Harthacnut travelled to England', 'landing at Sandwich on 17 June'; he had been king of Denmark since 1035 ('In 1035, Harthacnut succeeded his father on the throne of Denmark as Cnut III.') and his English reign runs 1040 to 8 June 1042.

8 June 1042: England leaves the union at Harthacnut's death. H1: 'On 8 June 1042, Harthacnut attended a wedding in Lambeth', where he died; he 'was succeeded by Magnus in Denmark and Edward the Confessor in England'.
8 June 1042: Harthacnut dies and Denmark passes to Magnus of Norway. H1: 'Harthacnut died suddenly in 1042 and was succeeded by Magnus in Denmark and Edward the Confessor in England.'

certainty.note: A union of two crowns across the North Sea; each kingdom's old frontiers, none fixed by treaty on the pages opened.

notes:
DECISION: Denmark-England is Harthacnut's union of the two crowns from June 1040 to his death in June 1042, ending three years before Cliopatria's 1045. It is kept as its own dossier because Cnut's union broke in 1035 (see north-sea-empire) and this one re-forms without Norway; the colour agent may prefer to give it the North Sea Empire's colour. The article on the North Sea Empire counts Harthacnut as the empire's last ruler (infobox 1040-1042).
CLIOPATRIA GAPS FOUND: no Kingdom of England shape 1018-1045 (England 1043-1045 is drawn by this row), no Danish row 1018-1055 (Denmark 1043-1045 is drawn by this row; it belongs with Magnus, norway-denmark). The kingdom-of-england dossier (eu-11 or 10) and the denmark dossiers should be told.
WIKIPEDIA TITLE: Cliopatria gives 'Danish attacks on Norman England' (Wikidata Q111953993); that article starts with Cnut's empire and Sweyn Estridsson's claim and runs to 1240; it has no 1040-1045 dates (H2). The dossier's identity uses it as given.
NO WAR: none moved the border inside 1040-1042. Harthacnut's quarrel with Magnus of Norway predates the union: H1 has Magnus invading in 1035, forcing Sweyn and Ælfgifu to flee, and a treaty that whichever king died without an heir would be succeeded by the other (dated 1036 by Howard, 1039 by other historians); Magnus took Denmark in 1042 under it. Capital unverified; no area on either page. Pages used: 2 of 2.
